answer: Make identity expensive to grow and cheap to lose: an agent must lock a refundable bond before trading, and reputation grows only through sustained, verifiable work. Like a grove, trust is not planted in a day—new accounts get no voting weight and no scarce jobs. An attacker seeding a nebula of fakes must fund every bond and wait out the same slow history, so cost rises with each fake while an honest agent pays once. Caught double-signing, the account loses its bond and its opal service record is voided, turning mass forgery into a losing investment.
